We have search results. Need to find template that when applied retrosynthetically (i.e., reverse of forward) to target molecule reproduces reaction described: cycloaddition forming ring, C-C bond formed, C-O bond broken, loss of ketone and C-C triple bond functional groups. The target molecule: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. This is a methyl ester? Actually COC( ... )=O is methyl ester of something. Contains a carbonyl (ketone? actually ester). Also contains a silyl group attached to a cyclopropene? C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclopropene with silyl substituent. Also a conjugated double bond to phenyl.

The forward reaction: cycloaddition between two unsaturated parts forming a cyclic product, losing ketone and C-C triple bond. So retrosynthetic step: break a C-C bond (new sigma) and break a C-O bond (original carbonyl? Actually carbonyl broken). The template likely involves a [2+2] or [4+2] cycloaddition? The search result includes first entry reaction_id 1914386 with retro_smarts_template that seems to involve a C#C triple bond and a carbonyl (ketone). Let's examine that entry: retro_smarts_template: '[C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D3;+0:13]1=[CH;D2;+0:14]-[C;H0;D4;+0:1]-1(/[CH;D2;+0:2]=[CH;D2;+0:3]/[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8]>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8].[C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D2;+0:13]#[CH;D1;+0:14]'

This seems to be a retro Diels-Alder? It splits a product with a carbonyl and a triple bond into two fragments: one is a carbonyl-containing chain, the other is a silyl-substituted alkyne? The product side (left of >>) is O=[C...]-... plus a silyl alkyne fragment. The mapped_rxn shows product: [CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]... and O=[C:5]... So the product is the target? The mapped_rxn product side is the target? Let's see mapped_rxn: '[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19].O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

So reactants (left) are alkyne with silyl and a carbonyl chain (ester). Product (right) is the target molecule (with cyclopropene? Actually product shows [CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si...] which is a cyclopropene? The product includes a C=C double bond to Si? Actually it's a cyclopropene? The product is the target: methyl ester attached to a cyclopropene fused to phenyl? The product SMILES matches our target? Let's compare: target: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. The product SMILES in mapped_rxn: [CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]. That matches: methyl ester (COC(=O) ), a cyclopropene (C1(C=C1[Si]...), attached to a phenyl via a double bond. Yes matches target.

Thus this template (template_id?) We have reaction_id 1914386, template_hash, but need template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The search result includes 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash'. The template_id likely is reaction_id? Or there is separate template_id field? In description, search returns list of templates each with details, including maybe 'template_id'? The result shows 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash', 'retro_smarts_template', etc. The template_id likely is 'reaction_id' (since they refer to template ID). We'll assume template_id = 1914386.

We need to return mapped_rxn string and template_id integer.

Mapped_rxn from entry: '[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19].O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

Thus final answer.
